metrics.name: Yield
metrics.zero_behavior: Yield = 0 when cache_read = 0 or output = 0 (and input > 0)
metrics.missingness_behavior: null when input = 0 or cache_read is null
metrics.aggregation_behavior: Compute from aggregated sums, not averaged from per-request values
metrics.normalization_profile: None normative in v0.1. Proposed profiles in metrics/normalization-profiles.md: window-normalized (Υ_w), linear-input (Υ_lin), sqrt-input (Υ_sqrt), log-yield (log_Υ). All experimental, deferred to v0.2 via OEP.
metrics.interpretation: A composite signal combining cache reuse (Leverage) and output generation (Velocity). Higher values indicate more output per unit of fresh input, amplified by cache reuse.
metrics.prohibited_interpretation: Must not be presented as proof of code quality, productivity, task success, employee performance, or business impact.
known_limitations: Quadratically sensitive to input scale due to input² in denominator
Non-monotonic: doubling both input and output (same ratio) halves Yield if cache_read is constant
Not comparable across observation windows of different granularity without disclosure
security_gaming_considerations: An operator can inflate Yield by maximizing cache_read (reusing cached context) while minimizing fresh input
An operator can inflate Yield by generating verbose output
Anti-gaming is a platform-layer concern, not a protocol concern

metrics.name: Leverage
metrics.missingness_behavior: null when input = 0 or cache_read is null
metrics.aggregation_behavior: Compute from aggregated sums, not averaged from per-request values
metrics.normalization_profile: None normative in v0.1. See metrics/normalization-profiles.md for proposed profiles.
metrics.interpretation: How much cached context an operator reuses relative to fresh input. Higher values indicate greater cache utilization.
metrics.prohibited_interpretation: Must not be presented as proof of skill, productivity, or efficiency in any absolute sense.
known_limitations: Sensitive to provider caching policy: providers with aggressive caching will produce higher Leverage
Not comparable across providers without adapter disclosure
Can be gamed by artificially reducing fresh input
security_gaming_considerations: An operator can inflate Leverage by minimizing fresh input tokens (e.g., very short prompts with large cached context)
Provider caching policy changes can cause artificial Leverage shifts unrelated to operator behavior

metrics.name: Velocity
metrics.missingness_behavior: null when input = 0. Does not require cache fields.
metrics.aggregation_behavior: Compute from aggregated sums, not averaged from per-request values
metrics.normalization_profile: None normative in v0.1. See metrics/normalization-profiles.md for proposed profiles.
metrics.interpretation: How much output an operator generates relative to fresh input. Higher values indicate more output per unit of fresh input.
metrics.prohibited_interpretation: Must not be presented as proof of output quality, usefulness, or task success. High Velocity may indicate verbose, low-quality output.
known_limitations: Does not account for output quality
Sensitive to task type: code generation tasks may produce different Velocity than explanation tasks
Can be gamed by generating verbose output
security_gaming_considerations: An operator can inflate Velocity by generating unnecessarily verbose output
An operator can inflate Velocity by minimizing fresh input (short prompts)

metrics.name: output_fraction
metrics.missingness_behavior: null when input + output = 0. Does not require cache fields.
metrics.aggregation_behavior: Compute from aggregated sums, not averaged from per-request values
metrics.normalization_profile: None normative in v0.1. See metrics/normalization-profiles.md for proposed profiles.
metrics.interpretation: What fraction of total token flow (input + output) is output. A value of 0.9 means 90% of tokens are output.
metrics.prohibited_interpretation: Must not be presented as a signal-to-noise ratio. The name 'SNR' is a legacy alias and is misleading. This is an output fraction, not a signal-to-noise measure.
known_limitations: Does not distinguish between useful and verbose output
A high output_fraction does not indicate high-quality output
The legacy name 'SNR' implies signal-processing semantics that this formula does not have
security_gaming_considerations: An operator can inflate output_fraction by generating verbose output
An operator can inflate output_fraction by minimizing fresh input

metrics.name: log_leverage
metrics.zero_behavior: Not applicable: requires all four pillars > 0. Zero in any pillar → null.
metrics.missingness_behavior: null when any of input, output, cache_write, cache_read is zero or null
metrics.aggregation_behavior: Compute from aggregated sums, not averaged from per-request values
metrics.normalization_profile: None normative in v0.1. log_Υ = log_leverage + log10(Velocity) proposed in metrics/normalization-profiles.md as experimental.
metrics.interpretation: Logarithmic scale of cache reuse leverage. Compresses the wide dynamic range of Leverage into a more interpretable scale.
metrics.prohibited_interpretation: Must not be presented as a '10x developer' classification or developer productivity measure. The name '10xDEV' is a legacy alias that implies productivity, which the protocol explicitly disclaims.
known_limitations: Requires all four pillars > 0, making it undefined for many real-world observations
The reference implementation policy (all four pillars > 0) is stricter than the mathematical requirement (only input > 0 and cache_read > 0)
The '10xDEV' label creates a false implication of developer productivity classification
security_gaming_considerations: Same gaming opportunities as Leverage, compressed to a log scale
The '10xDEV' name may incentivize gaming to reach a '10x' threshold
